item.title: Four-Dimensional Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones: A Complete Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.00101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all four-dimensional semi-homogeneous convex cones, i.e., closed, pointed, full-dimensional cones whose connected automorphism group has principal orbits of codimension at most one. On such cones, the Monge-Amp\`ere equation defining the canonical barrier reduces to an ordinary differential equation. This makes this barrier computationally accessible. The semi-homogeneous cones can then be used in modeling by conic programs. An obvious subset of such cones are the homogeneous cones. The key point allowing the classification is that for all other cones, the automorphism group has a three-dimensional subgroup acting locally faithfully on the principal orbits. This subgroup must have a Lie algebra which is either abelian or a direct product of a 1-dimensional algebra and a two-dimensional algebra generated by $A,B$ satisfying $[A,B]=B$. In both cases we classify all 4-dimensional representations up to isomorphism, and for each representation all invariant convex cones. For every cone an orbit invariant is computed.
item.dc:creator: Amir Valiakhmetov, Ewsey Obzherin, Alexey Chernov, Roland Hildebrand

item.title: Blowdowns along Ricci flow in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2611.00139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the blowdown shrinking Ricci soliton of Feldman, Ilmanen and Knopf is strictly dynamically stable in the following strong local sense: (1) The Ricci flow from every metric on a closed 4-manifold containing a region close to a rescaling of a sufficiently large compact subset of the soliton in either orientation and with controlled geometry elsewhere develops a singularity with unique tangent flow modeled on the soliton. (2) The singular time slice has an isolated conical singularity, and by Gianniotis-Schulze the flow can be continued by blowing down a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (3) On a closed 4-manifold, the set of metrics whose Ricci flows have their first singularity modeled on the soliton is $C^{14}$-open. It is nonempty if and only if the manifold contains a sphere of self-intersection $\pm1$. (4) The soliton is strongly rigid among shrinking Ricci solitons. As applications, we construct $C^{14}$-open sets of initial data whose Ricci flows perform any prescribed ordered sequence of blowdowns. (1) Every closed simply connected smooth 4-manifold, including spin and exotic examples, can be reached by Ricci flow from a standard $k\mathbb{CP}^2\#\ell\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2$, through finitely many blowdown singularities. (2) On the standard $2\mathbb{CP}^{2}\#9\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^{2}$, there are infinitely many open sets of initial metrics whose Ricci flows, after a single blowdown, reach pairwise nondiffeomorphic manifolds. The proof uses the spectral analysis of Naff and the second author and deals with the gauge-fixing problem along Ricci flow through a Wa\.zewski argument inspired by Stolarski. We also use Bamler-Lai's PDE-ODI principle. Except for continuation (requiring nonnegative curvature of the asymptotic cone), all results apply to linearly stable nonflat asymptotically conical shrinkers in all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Dain Kim, Tristan Ozuch

item.title: Noncritical multi-bubbles and hyperbolic double bubbles
item.description: arXiv:2611.00252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that standard $k$-bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$ for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and that standard double bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb H^n$ for $n\ge3$. For nonnegative curvature, the proof combines the structure and spectral theory of Milman--Neeman with a uniform semialgebraic exceptional set, an almost-everywhere profile comparison, and localized variational arguments. A curvature-variable lift gives a uniformly elliptic comparison at the Euclidean limit. The independent hyperbolic argument uses the rotational structure of Cotton--Freeman, a scalar meridian force potential, and a transverse conformal variation. The critical range $k=n+1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$, and hyperbolic clusters with more than two finite cells, are not covered.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Wang

item.title: A Koszul-Type Splitting Theorem for Complex Supermanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.00331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the splitting problem for complex supermanifolds using formal exponential maps and Ehresmann connections. We show that every formal exponential map induces a splitting of the underlying supermanifold. Furthermore, we establish that every Ehresmann connection determines a linearization of the infinite jet space, extending the corresponding construction for ordinary manifolds to supermanifolds. For Ehresmann connections preserving the zero section, we construct a formal exponential map in two ways: via the linearization of the infinite jet space and directly from the connection operator. We prove that both constructions yield the same map and induce the same splitting, thereby generalizing Koszul's splitting theorem from linear connections to zero-section-preserving Ehresmann connections. Finally, we provide examples showing that, without this assumption, the two constructions may yield different splittings, or one or both of them may fail to induce a splitting.
item.dc:creator: Luiz F. A. Campos, Alexey Sharapov, Elizaveta Vishnyakova

item.title: Coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes I: (3,2)-Kinematical Lie algebras with $d\geq 3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is the first of several papers devoted to the classification of coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes. It is the first step in extending the classification of spatially isotropic homogeneous spacetimes of kinematical Lie groups to the much vaster context of homogeneous spacetimes that are not spatially isotropic; that is, where the rotations no longer act transitively on the space of directions in each tangent space. In this first paper we classify (up to isomorphisms preserving the rotational subalgebra) a class of the relevant transitive Lie algebras, the so-called (3,2)-kinematical Lie algebras, for the coisotropy-one case in spatial dimension at least 4. As a by-product of this classification, we classify two-dimensional real representations of Bianchi Lie algebras up to a suitable notion of equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'{e} Miguel Figueroa-O'Farrill, Juan Manuel Lorenzo-Naveiro

item.title: The Continuum Limit of the Deep Linear Network
item.description: arXiv:2611.00503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Deep Linear Network (DLN) is a simple version of a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) in which the activation function is the identity and the bias vector is the zero vector. We examine the behavior of the model when the number of weight matrices, which is finite in the original model, goes to infinity. We show that a plausible continuum limit is a dimensionally reduced version of the Yang-Mills equation on the torus, revealing an unexpected geometric interpretation of infinite-depth DLNs. While we do not prove this rigorously, it is a very pretty calculation. It also gives some insight into several features of the construction. We note that the choices of boundary conditions on the ends of the discrete series survive better in the continuum limit. Also, the regularizing functional which uses the moment map survives nicely in the continuum limit, whereas the regularizing functional using the size of approximating terms has no sensible limit. This surely is useful information for the choices we make in the finite-dimensional theory, and might also be useful in the more complicated MLP setting.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Eva Pfaff, Karen Uhlenbeck

item.title: A closed formula for the Poisson cohomology of scalar Dubrovin-Novikov brackets in arbitrary dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.00531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The structure of the Poisson cohomology groups for scalar Poisson brackets of Dubrovin-Novikov type with $D$ independent variables has been first described in arXiv:1512.05744 ; in that work, a complete dimensional counting was provided for $D=2$, and some numerical results exhibited for $D=3$, $D=4$. Here, we prove a formula for the dimensional counting of the Poisson cohomology for arbitrary $D$. Moreover, we show how to obtain canonical representatives for each cohomology class.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Casati

item.title: Spectral and convex geometry of $\alpha$-harmonic maps and sharp Morse index rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.00642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a weighted scalar spectral geometric description of Sacks-Uhlenbeck $\alpha$-harmonic maps into round spheres and identify its convex geometry realization for $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere. More precisely, we establish a one-to-one correspondence, modulo orientation preserving isometries of $\mathbb{S}^2$, between orientation preserving $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere and positive Codazzi tensors satisfying a determinant bound and a compatibility condition with the prescribed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$. These tensors are the radii tensors of auxiliary strictly convex surfaces, and the weighted scalar forms in spectral geometry equal $-\alpha$ times the second variations of the enclosed volumes with respect to the support functions. Using these spectral geometry and convex geometry results, we prove a sharp Morse index characterization of isometric equatorial parametrizations among $\alpha$-harmonic $2$-spheres in the round $n$-sphere. We also prove that every $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphism between unit round $2$-spheres is orthogonal for all $\alpha>1$. Equivalently, the only admissible positive Codazzi tensor whose reconstructed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has Gaussian curvature $1$ is $(\kappa+2)^{\alpha-1}\bar{g}$, where $\bar{g}$ is the unit round metric.
item.dc:creator: Rui Gao, Miaomiao Zhu

item.title: On the Local Regularity of Homogeneous Complex Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.00736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a local higher regularity theorem for the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampere equation on $X\times D$, where $X$ is a complete, possibly noncompact Kahler manifold and $D\subset\mathbb C$ is the unit disc. For a bounded weak solution given by the Perron envelope, we prove higher regularity on a smaller spatial domain when the smooth boundary data are locally small. The geometric hypotheses require uniformly convex local Kahler potentials and a local barrier threshold sufficiently large relative to the global $L^\infty$ bound of the solution. We also obtain quantitative local Holder estimates. The proof combines a perturbative construction of local holomorphic disc foliations with a construction of global subsolutions using convexity and barriers. A key analytic difficulty is the loss of Holder regularity in the construction of holomorphic disc families, which we address using BMO estimates and Nash-Moser-Zehnder theorems. Comparison along the discs identifies the local smooth solution by holomorphic discs foliation with the global weak solution. We apply the theorem and its proof to compact Kahler manifolds and to ALE, ALF, and asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) ends. Under the stated geometric and decay assumptions, we obtain higher regularity of each prescribed order sufficiently far out, together with weighted Holder estimates preserving the boundary decay.
item.dc:creator: Qi Yao

item.title: Spatial degeneracy along weak geodesics in the space of K\"ahler potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.00744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spatial Hessian degeneracy along weak K\"ahler geodesics. We construct examples in three settings: (1) On every compact K\"ahler manifold, the spatial form degenerates on a nonempty open set during an interior time interval, although both endpoints are smooth and strictly K\"ahler. (2) On ALE K\"ahler manifolds with a holomorphic quotient end and a decaying potential to the Euclidean metric, spatial degeneracy occurs on open regions arbitrarily far along an unbounded horn. (3) For cone and Poincar\'e endpoint metrics along a smooth divisor, normal spatial degeneracy occurs on open sets approaching the divisor. Both cone endpoints retain the prescribed angle. The first construction answers negatively the spatial-positivity question recorded in Darvas's survey. The ALE and divisor constructions show that weak geodesics need not preserve the asymptotic behavior of the endpoint metrics.
item.dc:creator: Xia Xiao, Qi Yao

item.title: Biunital Lie Semiheaps and Lie Triple Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the differential geometry of Lie semiheaps that admit biunital elements. Open Ol'shanskii semigroups, which appear widely across causal geometry and harmonic analysis, provide a large class of examples. It is shown that the subset of biunits is a smoothly embedded Lie subheap. Moreover, there is a canonical Lie triple algebroid associated with any proper biunital Lie semiheap. That is, there is a vector bundle over the manifold of biunits that comes equipped with a ternary bracket that satisfies the axioms of a Lie triple system together with a compatible `higher' anchor map. Although every Lie triple algebroid associated with a proper biunital Lie semiheap is trivialisable, it is not canonically so, unlike the case of the tangent bundle of a Lie group. As concrete examples, we examine the Lie semiheap of real $n\times n$ matrices, and the conformal causal Lie semiheap associated with the Lie group $\mathrm{SU}(2,2)$, which is a double cover of the conformal group of Minkowski spacetime, and the future-directed light cone.
item.dc:creator: Andrew James Bruce

item.title: Metric Correspondences and Low-Rank Deformations for Conformal and \(m\)-Modified Conformal Vector Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.00844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We fix a smooth vector field and a positive parameter $m$, and compare the nondegenerate metrics for which the field is conformal or $m$-modified conformal with the same prescribed smooth factor. Metrics of arbitrary signature are allowed. Passing to inverse metrics gives a linear transport equation and an explicit correspondence on the exact nondegeneracy domains. At a regular point, transverse initial data yield a signature-preserving correspondence of metric germs. For a nowhere-zero field and a Killing background in dimension at least three, every metric satisfying the modified conformal equation and differing from the background by a tensor of rank at most one has factor zero; its inverse-metric difference is $rX\otimes X$ for a unique smooth function $r$. Under a complete flow, such global deformations exist precisely when the field is null for the background and admits a smooth function $\tau$ with $X\tau=1$. An auxiliary field satisfying $[X,Z]=X$ gives a second correspondence under orthogonality assumptions. Finally, for a nowhere-zero complete field, a Killing metric and a zero-factor modified conformal metric have inverse-metric difference of rank at least two whenever that rank is constant. In the rank-two case, the pair determines a unique auxiliary field. Examples distinguish the roles of dimension, completeness, constant rank, the zero-factor condition, and orthogonality.
item.dc:creator: Zhigang Li

item.title: Curvature pinching for minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in spheres
item.description: arXiv:2611.00976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a rigidity theorem for closed connected minimal Tangent-Yang-Mills hypersurfaces in the unit sphere. In every dimension $n\geqslant 3$, such a hypersurface is totally geodesic if the squared norm of its Riemannian curvature tensor is at most $2n(n-1)$.
item.dc:creator: Jianquan Ge, Lixin Xiao, Wenjin Zhang

item.title: Locally Conformal Analysis of Non-Degenerate Odd Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.00982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the locally conformal geometry of cosymplectic and coorientable contact manifolds within a common algebraic framework based on a non-degenerate odd pair: a one-form and a two-form whose appropriate wedge product defines a nowhere-vanishing top-degree form on an odd-dimensional manifold. We consider conformally compatible local geometric and Hamiltonian data and encode their gluing through a closed Lee form and the Lichnerowicz-de Rham differential. For locally conformal cosymplectic geometry, we introduce an equal-weight formulation in which the defining forms carry the same conformal weight. This formulation allows compatible local Hamiltonian vector fields to glue directly into a global Hamiltonian vector field without additional rescaling, thereby preserving the local dynamics. For contact geometry, we develop a twisted odd-pair formulation in which the Lee form records the conformal gluing of local Hamiltonian data, while the global one-form remains an ordinary contact form. We illustrate these constructions through time-dependent mass dynamics in the cosymplectic setting and dissipative particle dynamics in the contact setting.
item.dc:creator: Beg\"um Ate\c{s}li, Aybike \c{C}atal-\"Ozer, O\u{g}ul Esen

item.title: Common-Source Assembly for Spherical Minimal Immersions
item.description: arXiv:2611.00984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a matching principle for assembling maps from a common manifold into spherical minimal immersions. The equations couple the coefficients to the induced metric and yield examples with nonminimal constituent immersions. We establish existence and uniqueness of matching coefficients under suitable hypotheses and sharp rigidity for complete harmonic assemblies over $\mathbb S^2$. For a Clifford family, the first eigenspace determines the underlying fibration. The principle also produces weighted minimal profiles that generate minimal products in round spheres, with examples formed from finitely many Lawson--Osserman blocks of different degrees over a common Hopf source.
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Zhang

item.title: Stratified Superintegrability of Spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Poisson chain of the compact spin Calogero-Moser-Sutherland system obtained by conjugation reduction of $T^*\mathrm{SU}(n)$ at a fixed coadjoint orbit. We give a Horn-type condition ensuring that the spectral torus acts freely on the full fiber over a simple spectrum; for each orbit, the admissible spectra form a nonempty open dense set, and the restricted chain is strongly superintegrable of rank $n-1$ on every orbit-type stratum. We also construct, across certain affine spectral walls, a proper quotient map onto a Hausdorff stratified Poisson space with a finite Whitney stratification. For $\mathrm{SU}(3)$, we compute the free spectral domain and the quotient near two intersecting walls, and a zero-orbit example shows that the analogous quotient need not be Hausdorff on the unrestricted reduced phase space.
item.dc:creator: Guorui Ma, Junze Zhang

item.title: Optimal AB-program for Poincar\'e--Sobolev and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that we can subtract the full spectral gap $\left(\frac{N-1}{p}\right)^{p}$ of the $p$-Laplacian and keep the sharp Sobolev constant $S(N,p)$ of $\mathbb{R}^N$ at the same time in a large family of $p$. For $p=2$, this was proved by Benguria, Frank and Loss in dimension three, and it was shown by Hebey to be false in dimensions $N\geq4$. For $p\neq2$, it was proved by Nguyen for $N\geq4$ and $\frac{2N}{N-1}\leq p<N$. By employing, among other tools, a suitable conjugation that maps the radial $p$-Dirichlet integral on $\mathbb{H}^N$ onto its Euclidean counterpart on $\mathbb{R}^N$ while preserving the $L^p$ norm, together with a one-dimensional tangent line inequality, we establish such sharp Poincar\'e--Sobolev inequalities for $N=3$ and $2\leq p<3$, for $N=4$ and $\frac{1+\sqrt{13}}{2}\leq p<4$, and for $N\geq5$ and $\min\{3,\frac{1+\sqrt{4N-3}}{2}\}\leq p<N$. In particular, in all cases we also obtain an explicit remainder term. Moreover, since the change of function keeps the $L^p$ norm, we prove the sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with the full spectral gap and the sharp Euclidean constant for $N=3$ and $2\leq p\leq3$, and for $N\geq4$ on an explicit interval of $p$. For $p\geq3$, we also use the change of variable $t=\sinh\rho$ and the Hardy inequality, which give a second remainder term. At the endpoint $p=N$, this remainder gives a Hardy--Trudinger--Moser inequality on $\mathbb{H}^N$ under a weaker constraint than the one of Liang, Lu, Wang and Yang, in every dimension $N\geq3$. Finally, we show that for $1<p<\frac{1+\sqrt{4N-3}}{2}$, which includes all $1<p<2$, the full spectral gap can still be subtracted with some positive constant in front of the Sobolev term, and that this constant is smaller than $S(N,p)^{p}$ when $p<\min\{2,\sqrt N\}$. Together with our other results, this shows that the full spectral gap can be subtracted for every $1<p<N$.
item.dc:creator: Anh Do, Debdip Ganguly, Nguyen Lam, Guozhen Lu

item.title: Triple bubbles in the hyperbolic plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.01367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the standard triple bubble uniquely minimizes perimeter among clusters in the hyperbolic plane with three prescribed positive finite areas. The standard family admits global pressure coordinates, and its volume differential is the negative of a positive definite grounded weighted graph Laplacian. A normalized perimeter excess attains a comparison minimum under a perimeter bound and gives a strict comparison between actual and model pressures. Component relabeling reduces the possible topologies to an all-boundary network or a 4-daisy. Discrete comparisons exclude the 4-daisy; pressure-preserving face deletion reduces the remaining network to the standard tetrahedral configuration.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Wang

item.title: Degenerate neckpinches at the first $N$ singular times
item.description: arXiv:2611.01419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every integer $N\ge1$, we construct a smooth closed connected strictly mean-convex rotationally symmetric surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose level set flow remains connected until extinction and has exactly one singular point at each of its first $N$ singular times. These singularities are degenerate neckpinches with the Angenent--Vel\'azquez asymptotics: the leading deviation from the cylinder under parabolic rescaling is a cubic Hermite term.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: Cosmological rigidity via $p$-harmonic temporal functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.
item.dc:creator: Argam Ohanyan

item.title: Spectral gaps near one quarter for Weil--Petersson random surfaces with growing cusp number
item.description: arXiv:2611.01477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ with $n=n(g)\ge1$ labelled cusps converges in probability to $1/4$ as $g\to\infty$, for every sequence $n=o(\sqrt g)$. More precisely, for each fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, there are constants $C_\varepsilon\ge2$ and $g_\varepsilon\ge3$, independent of $n$, such that the expected number of nonzero $L^2$ eigenvalues in $(0,1/4-\varepsilon]$, counted with multiplicity and including residual eigenvalues, is at most $C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2/g$ whenever $g\ge g_\varepsilon$ and $g\ge C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2$. This proves a conjecture of Shen and Wu. A matching lower bound shows that the count estimate is optimal up to constants for each fixed $\varepsilon$, and that $n=o(\sqrt g)$ is necessary for convergence of the gap to $1/4$. The proof combines volume estimates uniform in the cusp count with polynomial approximation and a positive trace on truncated surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Guan Huang

item.title: Topping's diameter conjecture for immersed surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve Topping's diameter conjecture for closed immersed surfaces in Euclidean three-space, building on his recent result for embedded surfaces. More generally, we establish sharp diameter and mean-width estimates for compact connected immersed surfaces, possibly with boundary. As a consequence, we confirm the codimension-one case of the sharp length--diameter conjecture for immersed minimal surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Miura

item.title: Double Fibration Transforms: Geometry and Microlocal Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.01760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double fibration transforms integrate functions over families of submanifolds. We survey the recovery of singularities by both classical normal operator methods and direct analytic methods. We also discuss support theorems, injectivity and applications to geodesic ray transforms, seismic inversion and minimal surface data.
item.dc:creator: Shubham R. Jathar, Jesse Railo

item.title: Convergence of the Calabi flow on K\"ahler surfaces with bounded Sobolev constants
item.description: arXiv:2611.01882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study global Calabi flows $g(t)$ on compact K\"ahler surfaces with a uniform Sobolev constant. For any sequence $t_j\to\infty$, set $g_j(t):=g(t_j+t)$. After passing to a subsequence, these flows converge to an eternal Calabi flow on a compact extremal K\"ahler orbifold surface. The convergence holds in the spacetime $\hat C^\infty$-Cheeger--Gromov topology: it is uniform in the Gromov--Hausdorff sense on compact time intervals and smooth away from the orbifold singularities, using comparisons fixed in time.
item.dc:creator: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang, Kai Zheng

item.title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2611.01912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hasegawa

item.title: Boundary fibers of the holonomy map for complex projective structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.01928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Morgan--Shalen boundary of holonomy representations of complex projective structures on a compact Riemann surface of genus at least two. We prove that every direction defined by a holomorphic quadratic differential with a multiple zero admits distinct projective marked length limits. Together with Dumas's uniqueness theorem for simple zeros, this gives a complete characterization of directions with unique limits. We also establish that no nonzero abelian length function can occur in the holonomy boundary of any such fixed surface, regardless of the limiting quadratic differential. Finally, we characterize all directional boundary fibers by a necessary-and-sufficient analytic condition involving valued representations and the holomorphic jet bundle underlying an oper.
item.dc:creator: Shiyu Cao, Sheng Tan

item.title: Calabi flow on polarized K\"ahler surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study global smooth Calabi flows on polarized K\"ahler surfaces $(M,L)$, assuming uniformly bounded Sobolev constants and the algebraic conditions $\chi(\mathcal O_M)=1$ and $c_1(M)\cdot c_1(L)>0$. Using the orbifold compactness theorem, we prove a uniform Bergman estimate, construct a normal test configuration for each geometric limit, and establish uniqueness of the extremal orbifold limit up to polarized holomorphic isometry. K-polystability then identifies the limit with the original surface and gives a constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metric. We also prove finite-group equivariant versions of these results. Independently of the flow, we obtain a uniform Bergman lower bound for polarized cscK surfaces with bounded volume and Sobolev constants and $|S|\leq1$. We illustrate the hypotheses with nonstationary flows near a product cscK metric on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ and near Calabi's non-cscK extremal metric on the first Hirzebruch surface. Their controlled-cone energy inequalities follow from elementary calculations and continuity.
item.dc:creator: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang, Kai Zheng

item.title: Generalized Ricci Solitons on Heisenberg and Oscillator Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.02062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that on a connected, simply-connected nilpotent Lie group, the notions of left-invariant generalized Ricci soliton, semi-algebraic and algebraic generalized Ricci soliton coincide. Moreover, every such soliton has harmonic torsion. We classify all algebraic solitons with positive definite metric on the five-dimensional Heisenberg algebra, the four-dimensional oscillator algebra and the four-dimensional split-oscillator algebra up to automorphisms and rescalings. We find that there is only a finite number of algebraic solitons, all of which have harmonic torsion.
item.dc:creator: Vicente Cort\'es, Shubham Dwivedi, Lorenz Jetter

item.title: Isometric Embeddings of Hyperk\"{a}hler $\mathrm{T}^*\mathbb{CP}^{n}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit $U(n)$-equivariant isometric embeddings $T^*\mathbb{CP}^{n-1} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^{n^4+2n^2-1}$, $n\ge 2$, with respect to Calabi's hyperk\"{a}hler metric on $T^*\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}$. To achieve this, we first construct a diffeomorphism from $T^*\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}$ onto the manifold of rank-1 projections in $M_n(\mathbb{C})$, such that the pullback of half of the trace-class norm is a K\"{a}hler potential for the hyperk\"{a}hler metric. We then use the Hilbert space structure of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ to produce the isometric embeddings into Euclidean space.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Lackman

item.title: The Non-Abelian X-Ray Transform on Simple Asymptotically Hyperbolic Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a gauge equivalence result for the non-Abelian X-ray transform with connection and Higgs field on simple 2-dimensional asymptotically hyperbolic spaces. Our approach is based on the construction of holomorphic integrating factors. To construct these, we analyze the geodesic X-ray transform on functions on simple asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds of general dimension and prove polyhomogeneous mapping properties and a surjectivity result for the adjoint.
item.dc:creator: Nikolas Eptaminitakis, Haim Grebnev

item.title: Uniqueness of self-shrinking ends asymptotic to a cylindrical cone
item.description: arXiv:2611.02303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C^m \subset \mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ be a regular embedded cone, where $n\geq 1$, and let $k\geq 1$. We prove that two smooth, connected, properly embedded self-shrinking ends whose blow-downs converge locally smoothly to the same cylindrical cone $C\times\mathbb{R}^k$ away from the axis $\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}^k$ must coincide. As a consequence, we obtain a rigidity result for complete self-shrinkers asymptotic to cylindrical cones. The proof uses Gaussian decay estimates and a sectorial Carleman estimate to establish backward uniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Yile Liu

item.title: The Large-$N$ Limit of Ricci curvature in the Zeitlin Model on the Torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.02323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Euler equations of hydrodynamics describe the motion of an ideal incompressible fluid. Arnold observed that their solutions are geodesics on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of the fluid domain, equipped with the $L^2$ metric, so that the curvature of this group governs how nearby fluid motions separate. Sectional curvature takes both signs, and Ricci curvature, its average over all directions, is the natural measure of which sign prevails, but in infinite dimensions the sum defining it diverges. When the fluid domain is the flat torus, we define Ricci curvature through Zeitlin's finite-dimensional models, which approximate the Euler equations by geodesic equations on the matrix groups $SU(N)$. We compute the Ricci curvature of these models exactly and prove that, normalized by dimension, it converges as $N \rightarrow \infty$ to an explicit integral. The limit is strictly negative in every Fourier mode and decreases logarithmically with the wavenumber, the behavior conjectured in \cite{lichtenfelz2026ricci} for the sphere. We also show that the diameter of $SU(N)$ in the Zeitlin metric grows at most linearly in $N$.
item.dc:creator: Leandro Lichtenfelz, Isabelle Raad, Justin Valletta

item.title: Riemannian convex bodies with a geodesic segment on the boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.02355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct compact convex bodies whose boundaries contain a nontrivial geodesic segment and are strictly convex elsewhere. The construction applies if sectional curvature is constant near a point, or if a normal Jacobi operator has a simple maximal eigenvalue. In particular, such a body exists in every smooth three-dimensional or four-dimensional Riemannian manifold.
item.dc:creator: Hongda Qiu

item.title: Ricci flows and bracket flows on twisted principal bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.02477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that Ricci flows of invariant metrics on twisted principal bundles with nilpotent fibres over \(S^1\) are immortal and type III. After normalisation and lift to the universal cover, a sequence of metrics converges in the Cheeger--Gromov topology to a homogeneous expanding Ricci soliton. The proof extends the bracket flow technique from homogeneous Ricci flows to invariant Ricci flows on twisted principal bundles.
item.dc:creator: Henry Wood

item.title: A counterexample to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.02718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1988, J.~M.~Lee conjectured that a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold admits a pseudo-Einstein contact form if and only if the real first Chern class of its holomorphic tangent bundle vanishes. The necessity of this condition was proved by Lee. We show that the condition is not sufficient: in every real dimension $2n+1\ge 5$ there is a compact connected strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$ with $c_1(\Tone)=0$ in $H^2(M;\Z)$ which admits no pseudo-Einstein contact form. The examples are boundaries of small strictly pseudoconvex neighborhoods of a section $D\cong B$ with negative normal bundle in a $\PP^1$-bundle $\PP(E_e)\to B$, where $B=C^n$ is a power of a curve of genus two and $E_e$ is a non-split extension of $\cO_B$ by an ample line bundle $L$ with $K_B\cong L^2$. More generally, if $K_B\cong L^m$, such a boundary admits a pseudo-Einstein contact form if and only if $(m-1)e=0$, where $e\in H^1(B,L)$ is the extension class; the obstruction is detected on the first infinitesimal neighborhood of $D$.
item.dc:creator: Dong Yuxin, Wang Haohao

item.title: Rigidity of shrinking Ricci solitons with low-dimensional focal sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, the focal set of the potential function of a complete gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, and that every complete five-dimensional gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature is rigid. The first result follows from a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the focal set. For the second, when the scalar curvature is twice the soliton constant, we prove that total geodesy implies rigidity through an integral identity on the level hypersurfaces; the case of scalar curvature three times the soliton constant is treated by a separate argument. As further applications, we combine our methods with the rigidity theorem in the recent preprint of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou to obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension when the scalar curvature is twice or three times the soliton constant, and under integral Weyl pinching for four-dimensional focal sets.
item.dc:creator: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Hor\'acio

item.title: On knotted self expanders of the mean curvature flow in $\R^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we produce many examples of knotted self expanders. For example, there is an expander isotopic to a trefoil knot with three half cylinders attached.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Mramor, Shengwen Wang

item.title: A Reilly approach to weighted curvature integral inequalities in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2611.02882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a polarized weighted Reilly identity and an exact deficit decomposition for weighted curvature integrals $I_j=\int_\Sigma VE_j~\mathrm{d}\mu$ in hyperbolic space, where $V=\cosh r$ and $E_j$ is the normalized $j$th mean curvature. For compact domains with smooth connected boundary, these yield $I_k^2\geq I_{k-1}I_{k+1}$ under intrinsic sub-staticity at $k=1$ and static convexity with $\kappa\in\Gamma_k\cap\overline{\Gamma}_{k+1}$ for $2\leq k\leq n-1$, with equality precisely for geodesic balls. Under $h\geq0$ and $Vh-V_\nu g\geq0$, log-concavity and a Euclidean mixed-volume representation recover the centered-ball comparisons conjectured by Hu and Li \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{HuLi}, allowing the weight center to lie outside the domain. Equality in these comparisons holds precisely for balls centered at the weight center.
item.dc:creator: Shengguang Bi, Yingxiang Hu

item.title: Singularities of Separation Coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2611.02939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study singularities of separation coordinates for geodesic flows of real-analytic two-dimensional (pseudo-)Riemannian metrics. We obtain a complete local classification of these singularities using the Nijenhuis operator associated with a quadratic first integral. The singular set is locally a smooth curve, an isolated point, or two transversely intersecting curves. We also show that orthogonal separation near one point of an analytic disk extends to a quadratic first integral on the entire disk and provide explicit separation coordinates near singularities.
item.dc:creator: Dinmukhammed Akpan

item.title: Limiting properties of Hermitian-Einstein metrics under variation of the K\"ahler class
item.description: arXiv:2611.03025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the behaviour of Hermitian-Einstein metrics on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact K\"ahler manifold, as the underlying K\"ahler metric varies and its K\"ahler class changes. In particular, if the bundle stops being stable at some point, the Hermitian-Einstein metrics blow up, and their rescaling can be used to construct a destabilizing subsheaf, following the argument of Uhlenbeck and Yau. Furthermore, we study the behaviour of Chern connections of these metrics, and show, that after passing to a subsequence, and applying suitable gauge transforms these connections converge, and identify the blow-up locus of their Uhlenbeck limit.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Klemyatin

item.title: Entropy and round-point convergence for the $\sigma_k$-curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.03249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$ contracts to a round point under the $\sigma_k$-curvature flow for $2\leq k\leq n-1$, without additional pinching or symmetry assumptions. After rescaling about the extinction point to mean width two, the hypersurfaces converge smoothly and exponentially in normalized time to the unit sphere. The proof is based on an entropy which is invariant under translations and dilations and admits a representation by weighted boundary areas of orthogonal projections. A strengthened Codazzi inequality yields its monotonicity. An upper bound for the entropy controls the inradius relative to the mean width, while its dissipation controls the spatial variation of the normalized speed. We also obtain two-sided curvature bounds at the natural extinction scale.
item.dc:creator: Tianci Luo, Yong Wei, Ruijia Zhang, Rong Zhou

item.title: Macroscopic scalar curvature bounds on graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp lower bounds for the lengths of balls in the universal covers of finite metric graphs. For a finite connected $d$-regular graph, with $d \geq 3$ and average edge length at most one, we show that, at every radius, the average length of balls centered at a vertex of the universal cover is at least that of a ball of the same radius in the equilateral $d$-regular tree. We extend this comparison to arbitrary finite connected graphs whose total length does not exceed that of an equilateral trivalent graph with the same cyclomatic number. In particular, we show that the maximal length of a ball centered at a vertex of the universal cover is bounded below by that of a ball of the same radius in the equilateral trivalent tree. This answers a question of the first author. Furthermore, equality at an integer radius forces all edges to have unit length in the regular case and, in the general case, forces the graph to be an equilateral trivalent graph after suppressing vertices of degree two. In contrast, rigidity fails at every noninteger radius.
item.dc:creator: Steve Karam, St\'ephane Sabourau

item.title: Higher dimensional Kleinian groups of small Hausdorff dimension are classical Schottky groups II
item.description: arXiv:2611.03335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is the higher dimensional continuation of our works on Hausdorff dimension of Kleinian groups \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020}. In this paper we prove that for all $r\ge 2$ there exists $\lambda_r>0$, which is independent of the dimension $N$ of the hyperbolic space, such that any finitely generated non-elementary torsion-free Kleinian group of $\Isom(\mathbb{H}^N)$ generated by $r$ elements with limit set of Hausdorff dimension $<\lambda_r$ is a classical Schottky group. For two generators the bound can be taken to be $1/3$. The proof relies on our previous works in \cite{Hou2010}, \cite{Hou2020} and on a metric carrier graph reduction. Our result can also be considered as the complete converse to the well-known theorem of Phillips-Sarnak \cite{PS} for spaces of any dimension $N$.
item.dc:creator: Yong Hou

item.title: A proof of the spectral rigidity for complex projective space
item.description: arXiv:2611.03536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a proof of a folklore conjecture that a compact K\"ahler manifold with the same scalar Laplace spectrum as complex projective space equipped with the Fubini--Study metric is holomorphically isometric to it. More generally, we prove that the spectrum of the Hodge Laplacian in any one fixed degree $p$ determines $\CP^n$ up to holomorphic isometry among compact connected K\"ahler manifolds, for every fixed pair of integers $(p,n)$ with $0\leq p\leq n$. Equality of a single Hodge spectrum first forces periodic geodesic flow and the integral cohomology ring of complex projective space. The ordinary first heat coefficient then identifies the total scalar curvature except on a Pell sequence of pairs. For those pairs, a clean wave-trace argument, a Krawtchouk estimate, and a mod-two projective-bundle obstruction determine the geodesic return holonomy. A canonical K\"ahler involution recovers a weighted first heat coefficient which is nonzero throughout the exceptional sequence. The Kobayashi--Ochiai theorem and a fixed-class second-heat-coefficient calculation complete the argument.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

item.title: $C^1$-rigidity of $\mathbb{H}^{p,q}$-convex cocompact representations of Gromov hyperbolic groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p>3$ and let $\Gamma$ be a non-elementary Gromov hyperbolic group with $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. We prove that every $\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$-convex cocompact representation $$ \rho:\Gamma\longrightarrow \mathrm{PO}_{p,3} $$ whose proximal limit set $\Lambda_\rho\subset\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$ is a $C^1$ submanifold preserves a totally geodesic copy of $\mathbb{H}^p\subset\mathbb{H}^{p,2}$. Consequently, $\Gamma/\ker \rho$ is virtually a cocompact lattice in $\mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^p)$. For odd $p$, we prove the same conclusion for every signature $(p,q)$ with $p>q\ge2$, under the same hypothesis $\partial_\infty\Gamma\cong\mathbb S^{p-1}$. Our methods combine dynamics, differential topology, and representation theory. The key new ingredient is to study the radicals of the semidefinite forms induced on the tangent spaces of the limit set. They form a continuous vector bundle of constant rank. The tangent action at attracting fixed points gives a bound, in terms of the radical rank, on the number of eigenvalues of an orthogonal lift whose modulus exceeds one. We then use the topology of the sphere and the representation theory of real algebraic groups to exclude the remaining possibilities. In arbitrary signature with $p>q$, these arguments already imply that a representation with a $C^1$ limit set cannot be Zariski dense.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Bogachev

item.title: Flexibility of Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions under metric variation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the surjectivity of the differential of the Laplace-Beltrami operator with respect to the metric parameter. We use the obtained results to prove that every small deformation of a nonconstant eigenfunction can be realized with a small perturbation of the metric. As a consequence, we prove that every generic property of smooth functions which is invariant under multiplication by a nonzero scalar is generic for eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, extending a result by Uhlenbeck.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Agrachev, Nicola Da Ponte, Antonio Lerario, Matteo Testa

item.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
item.description: arXiv:2611.01423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.
item.dc:creator: Baohua Fu

item.title: Logarithmic Sobolev and exponential inequalities for submanifolds in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01610v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for complete $C^{1,1}$ immersed submanifolds of dimension $m\ge2$ in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with sectional curvature at most $-b^2$. The inequality retains the Euclidean sharp constant after subtraction of $(m-1)^2b^2$ from the Fisher and mean-curvature energy; this coefficient is maximal for a lower bound uniform over $b\ge0$. For immersed surfaces, we prove both a finite-domain critical exponential inequality and a global Ruf-type inequality with a positive $L^2$ term. Both have potential $|H|^2-b^2$, exponent $16\pi$ and an absolute multiplicative constant, and follow from one geometric heat-kernel comparison. The exponent and curvature coefficient are optimal. We classify Gaussian equality in the logarithmic inequality and geometric equality in the higher-dimensional Nash consequence. All inequality constants are independent of the codimension.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma

item.title: Chern scalar curvature and finite-time singularities of the conformal Chern--Calabi flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.01623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On every unit-volume flat complex three-torus, we construct a solution of the volume-preserving conformal Chern--Calabi flow with a finite-time Chern Type-I singularity at any prescribed point. The full spatial supremum has an exact asymptotic coefficient, and prescribed rescalings converge to a complete nonflat radial shrinking solution. The positive part of Chern scalar curvature can remain arbitrarily small throughout the flow, as can each prescribed subcritical spatial curvature norm. We determine the punctured terminal metric, its one-point completion and unique nonflat tangent cone, and the terminal energy asymptotics. We also exclude Chern Type-II under a logarithmically improved critical weak $L^3$ bound on Chern scalar curvature, and prove a separate scale-invariant integral criterion involving first Chern--Ricci curvature. The constructed singular solutions satisfy both criteria.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma, Li Sheng

item.title: Covariant Calculus and Hamiltonian Flows for Nonlocal Wasserstein Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.01979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study nonlocal metrics on smooth positive probability densities on a closed manifold, induced by symmetric jump kernels and density-dependent mobilities. First, we introduce the density-variation operator to express the density derivatives of the Dirichlet form and kinetic energy. Second, we construct density and velocity-field representations of the tangent space and prove their isometric equivalence. We use the generator's pseudoinverse to derive Levi-Civita connections and covariant differentials in both representations. Third, we establish mechanical Hamiltonian dynamics in both tangent representations; an action principle and Legendre duality identify the Hamilton--Jacobi and covariant Newton equations; smooth negative gradient flows admit a zero-energy Hamiltonian lift. Entropy diffusion, nonlocal mean-field equations, Keller--Segel dynamics, and a nonlocal Vlasov equation illustrate the resulting calculus. For geometric-mean mobility, the Hopf--Cole transformation of the nonlocal Schr\"odinger bridge system and the Madelung transformation of the nonlocal Schr\"odinger equation yield hyperbolic and trigonometric phase energies, respectively. At zero momentum, both recover the metric kinetic energy to second order.
item.dc:creator: Yuanke Chen, Jinqiao Duan, Qiao Huang

item.title: Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-\'Emery Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.02010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $\epsilon>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\le\kappa m_-$. Under the Bakry--\'Emery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$ \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le C_0\exp\!\bigl(C_1\sqrt{K_-}\,R\bigr) \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R)),\qquad R>0, $$ where $C_0,C_1$ depend only on $\epsilon,\kappa$. If $d$ is the maximum combinatorial degree of the support graph, we further prove under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ the sharp volume growth bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R))\le m_-CR^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}$ for all $o$ and $R\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Yanlong Ding, Shiping Liu, Chiyu Zhou

item.title: $C^0$-inextendibility of a class of Vaidya spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2611.02133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the future $C^0$-inextendibility of a broad subclass of ingoing Vaidya spacetimes with positive mass function satisfying the weak energy condition, building on methods introduced and developed by Sbierski for the Schwarzschild spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Karim Mosani, Clemens S\"amann, Kharanshu N. Solanki

item.title: Schwarz Lemma in Quaternionic Setting and $\mathbb C^4$
item.dc:creator: Chris Connell, Matvei Libine

item.title: Generalized Quasi-Symmetric Nets: A Constructive Approach to the Equimodular Elliptic Type and to Flexible $m \times n$ Nets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quadrilateral meshes that flex with rigid planar faces are of interest to transformable architecture, rigid-foldable origami, and mechanical metamaterials. Their building blocks are flexible $3 \times 3$ nets, that is, Kokotsakis polyhedra with a quadrangular base, classified by Izmestiev. We study one of his types, the equimodular elliptic type, defined by three conditions on the flat angles, the third of them through Jacobi elliptic functions. We turn these conditions into equivalent algebraic ones, free of elliptic functions, which lead to the generalized quasi-symmetric nets (GQS-nets), polyhedra of this type that include the known elliptic quasi-symmetric nets. For every polyhedron of this type, we give a flexible polyhedron with the same flat angles and its flexion in closed form. From the simplest GQS-nets, we assemble arbitrarily large flexible $m \times n$ nets. Examples include nets that, at one position, form letters; further nets in the supplementary materials form digits or, seen along their rows, approximately follow the side silhouettes of a bunny and a fish. Unlike numerically computed mechanisms, these nets are exactly flexible. As an application, we design three such nets as transportable arch halls of 80 mm sandwich panels, which fold to fit through the door of a standard container or into the well of a low-bed semi-trailer, and we check them numerically under snow load and build a 1:20 model of one. Supplementary Mathematica notebooks verify the symbolic computations, a Python tool constructs the nets and checks them numerically, including for self-intersections, and further scripts recheck the halls.
item.dc:creator: Abdukhomid Nurmatov, Florian Rist, Jonathan Klein, Dominik L. Michels

item.title: The dual Orlicz-Minkowski problem for capillary hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study curvature flows for the dual Orlicz--Minkowski problem for strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. The prescribed function has the form $\phi(h)G(X)$, where $X=\nabla h+h\nu$ and $G$ may be nonradial and nonhomogeneous. For acute contact angles, the evenness assumption together with either of the two integral conditions yields a smooth weighted-volume-preserving flow for all $t>0$ and a smooth solution to the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation. Without the evenness assumption, two strict spherical-cap barriers yield the same conclusions for an unnormalized flow, whose limiting hypersurfaces solve the dual Orlicz--Minkowski equation with $c=1$. A uniform strict monotonicity condition under rescaling ensures uniqueness for $c=1$ and convergence of the unnormalized flow in any $C^k$ norm at an exponential rate. The problem considered here includes the capillary $L_p$-Minkowski and $L_p$ dual Minkowski problems as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Ya Gao

item.title: Estimates for Ratios of Low-Order Eigenvalues of the Laplacian with Muckenhoupt Weights on Euclidean Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.02701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study low-order eigenvalue ratio estimates for the Laplacian with Muckenhoupt $A_2$ weights. For weights bounded above and below, we prove a universal upper bound for $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ with constant $1 + \frac{4}{n}\,\frac{C}{c}$, linear in the ratio of the weight bounds, and recover the classical Payne-P\'{o}lya-Weinberger bound as a special case. For radial decreasing weights, we prove that the ball maximizes $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ among domains of equal volume, assuming that an admissible radial test function exists (Definition 5.8) and that on the ball the second eigenvalue is attained by the $l=1$ mode. The argument adapts the method of Ashbaugh--Benguria to the weighted setting via a weighted Chiti comparison theorem and a monotonicity property of the admissible radial test function (Definition 5.8). Higher-order eigenvalue ratios are estimated in terms of the $(n-1)$-Hausdorff measure of the boundary, under an explicit balance condition on the weight at the covering scale. The generalized Payne-P\'{o}lya-Weinberger conjecture for eigenvalue sums remains open in general; conditional results are presented for restricted families of domains.
item.dc:creator: Jing Mao, He-Jun Sun, Lingzhong Zeng

item.title: Capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.02732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$, we study the long-time existence and asymptotic behavior of an even normalized capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski flow in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$. When $pq\geq0$, the flow exists for all positive time and the evolving hypersurfaces converge smoothly along a sequence of times tending to infinity to a stationary solution of the normalized problem. If $p\neq q$, a dilation of the limit solves the unnormalized problem.
item.dc:creator: Jinrong Hu, Yingxiang Hu, Bo Yang

item.title: Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights
item.description: arXiv:2611.03064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies. When nonempty, its connected components form a torsor for the degree-zero cohomology of an associated weighted gauge complex, and its higher homotopy groups are computed by the higher cohomology of this complex.
item.dc:creator: Grigorios Giotopoulos

item.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.03124v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
item.description: arXiv:2611.03221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $\chi = 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $\tau = 1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
item.dc:creator: Alfie Jones

item.title: Human Variations on AI Mathematics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article is motivated by the OpenAI manuscripts "Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints" and "Log abundance in characteristic zero". We establish a jet comparison for metrics with minimal singularities and use it to prove a dlt-type extension theorem. Combined with geometric arguments from the latter manuscript, this yields an alternative analytic proof of its Theorem~3.1.
item.dc:creator: Junyan Cao, Mihai Paun

item.title: On a Class of Non-Local Elliptic-Transport Systems in Score-Guided Probability Flow on $SE(3)$: Score-Singularity Resolution, Space-Time ADN Shift, and Markov Mean-Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2611.03278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish mathematical foundations for optimal spatiotemporal vector fields governing continuous score-guided probability flows over bounded submanifolds $M \subset SE(3)$ on the Special Euclidean group $SE(3) \cong \mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$. Modeling dynamic density evolution via a score-perturbed Lie-algebraic continuity equation under zero-flux boundary conditions, we resolve the non-local score drift singularity $s(g,t) = \nabla_{SE(3)} \log \rho(g,t)$ as $\rho \rightarrow 0^+$ via weighted parabolic flux dissipation bounds. Using left-invariant exponential group mollifiers, we derive boundary-preserving DiPerna--Lions commutator estimates tracking structure constants $\{c_{ij}^k\}$. Second, interpreting the optimality system as a 7D space-time elliptic operator $L_{7D} = -\Delta_{SE(3)} - \partial_t^2$ with zero-order corner compatibility on $\partial M \times \{0,T\}$, we establish Agmon--Douglis--Nirenberg $W_p^2(Q_T)$ shift estimates tracking Lie algebra constants, boundary geometry $\|\partial M\|_{C^2}$, and Ricci curvature $\|Ric_{SE(3)}\|_{L^\infty}$, yielding a full $C^\infty(\overline{Q}_T)$ Schauder bootstrap expansion. Third, we extend this system to non-cooperative Markov Mean-Field Games (MFGs) on $SE(3)$, establishing score-guided Nash equilibria via Schauder--Tychonoff fixed points. Crucially, the constant diagonal Ricci curvature $Ric_{SE(3)} = \mathrm{diag}(0,0,0,1/2,1/2,1/2)$ from $SO(3)$ induces a sharp Bochner--Weitzenb\"ock spectral gap boost $\lambda_1(-\Delta_{SE(3)}) \ge \lambda_1(-\Delta_{\mathbb{R}^3}) + 1/2 > 0$. This positive rotational curvature enhances the Lie-algebraic Poincar\'e coercivity constant, demonstrating that intrinsic group curvature stabilizes score-guided flows against dispersion and expands the critical Nash uniqueness horizon $T_{SE(3)}^*$ beyond flat Euclidean limits.
item.dc:creator: Pilhwa Lee

item.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.03514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).
item.dc:creator: Tianzhi Hu, Runze Zhang

item.title: Inferring geometric structure from eigenfunction triple products
item.description: arXiv:2611.03619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article presents two converses to well-known observations regarding products of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on a closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. First, if $(M,g)$ is real-analytic, the coefficients in the eigenfunction expansion of a product of eigenfunctions decay exponentially. We show that such exponential decay in fact implies that $g$ is real-analytic. Second, it is clear that if $(M,g)$ is flat, there exists an eigenbasis for which the product of any two of its elements lies in the span of at most $N = N(M,g)$ elements. We prove that any manifold with such an eigenbasis must be flat. We then construct metrics on $\mathbb{S}^7$ that share an eigenbasis with the standard metric yet are not locally homogeneous, from which we deduce that homogeneity cannot be characterized solely in terms of the multiplicative structure of eigenfunctions.
item.dc:creator: Josef Greilhuber, Romain Speciel

item.title: Remark on non-contractible closed geodesics and homotopy groups
item.description: arXiv:2307.13877v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if the $m$-th homotopy group for $m \geq 2$ of a closed manifold has non-trivial invariants or coinvariants under the action of the fundamental group, then there exist infinitely many geometrically distinct closed geodesics for a $C^4$-generic Riemannian metric. If moreover there are infinitely many conjugacy classes in the fundamental group, then the same holds for every bumpy Riemannian metric. Finally, under a homological condition that can detect the non-triviality of the higher homotopy groups, the same conclusion holds for every Riemannian metric. All three conclusions extend to smooth, possibly non-reversible Finsler metrics. In the generic statement, the conclusion holds for $C^6$-topology; under the homological hypothesis, the conclusion holds for every smooth Finsler metric.
item.dc:creator: Egor Shelukhin, Jun Zhang

item.title: K\"{a}hler Solitons, Contact Structures, and Isoparametric Functions
item.description: arXiv:2310.11328v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many known examples of simply-connected gradient K\"{a}hler-Ricci solitons in real dimension four are toric, and the symmetry is intrinsically related to the potential function $f$ and the scalar curvature $\SS$. In this article, we consider the case that $f$ and $\SS$ are functionally dependent and deduce a complete classification, while the independence case is addressed elsewhere. The main theorem recovers all known examples of cohomogeneity one symmetry. We also discover a connection to the theory of isoparametric functions and contact geometry. Indeed, a key ingredient is a new characterization for a deformed Sasakian structure generalizing a classical result.
item.dc:creator: Hung Tran

item.title: Non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics of two summands
item.description: arXiv:2505.06631v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on a class of compact manifolds arising as double disk bundles, whose principal orbits split into two inequivalent irreducible summands. The proof uses a phase space barrier argument that yields a new obstruction to the existence of closed cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics, even when the principal orbits admit homogeneous Einstein metrics.
item.dc:creator: Hanci Chi

item.title: Holomorphic disks with boundary on compact Lagrangian surface
item.description: arXiv:2505.19407v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $L$ be a compact oriented Lagrangian surface in a K\"ahler surface endowed with a complete Riemannian metric (compatible with the symplectic structure and the complex structure) with bounded sectional curvatures and a positive lower bound on injectivity radius. We show that for every nontrivial class $[\gamma]$ of the fundamental group $\pi_1(L)$ such that $\gamma$ bounds a topological disk in $M$, there exists a holomorphic disk whose boundary belongs to $L$ and is freely homotopic to $\gamma$ on $L$. This answers a question of Bennequin on existence of $J$-holomorphic disks. Nonexistence of exact Lagrangian embeddings of certain surfaces is established in such K\"ahler surface if the fundamental form is exact. In the almost K\"ahler setting, especially, the cotangent bundles of compact manifolds, results on nonexistence of $J$-holomorphic disks and existence of minimizers of the partial energies in the sense of A. Lichnerowicz are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Jingyi Chen

item.title: Scalar and Mean Curvature Comparison on Compact Cylinder
item.description: arXiv:2507.07005v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $ X $ be a closed, oriented Riemannian manifold. Denote by $ (M = X \times I = X \times [0, 1], \partial M = X \times \lbrace 0 \rbrace \cup X \times \lbrace 1 \rbrace, g) $ a compact cylinder with smooth boundary, $ \dim M \geqslant 3 $. In this article, we address the following question: If $ g $ is a Riemannian metric having (i) positive scalar curvature (PSC metric) on $ M $ and nonnegative mean curvature on $ \partial M $; and (ii) $ \chi(X) = 0 $ and $ \dim X \geq 5 $, then there exists a PSC metric on $ X $. This generalizes a result of Gromov and Lawson for $ X = \mathbb{T}^{n} $. Our result also implies an infinite band width consequence complementary to Gromov's band width conjecture, which roughly says no additional obstruction or flexibility for the existence of PSC on $ X $ is gained by passing to $ X \times [0, 1] $. Our result relies on geometric PDE analysis with respect to a new conformal invariance---the $ g $-angle condition between normal vector field along $ \partial M $ and the global vector field tangential to the $ I $-direction.
item.dc:creator: Jie Xu

item.title: General Chen's first inequality and applications for Riemannian maps
item.description: arXiv:2510.10505v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose \textit{general Chen's first inequality} for Riemannian maps between Riemannian manifolds and demonstrate its equality and sharpness via non-trivial examples. We also utilize this general inequality by establishing Chen's first inequalities when the target spaces are generalized complex and generalized Sasakian space forms, including real, complex, real K\"ahler, Sasakian, Kenmotsu, cosymplectic, and almost $C(\alpha)$ space forms. In addition, we estimate $\delta$-invariants under various hypotheses on these space forms. Finally, we validate our new approach by comparing particular results with those of existing approaches.
item.dc:creator: Ravindra Singh, Kiran Meena, Kapish Chand Meena

item.title: Stability of Homogeneous minimal hypersurfaces in the Page space and $Y^{p,q}$ Sasaki-Einstein manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2511.05447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the stability of homogeneous minimal submanifolds in two families of closed Einstein manifolds, the Page space $\mathbb{CP}^2 \# \overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ and the Sasaki-Einstein spaces $Y^{p,q}$, which are equipped with cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics admitting the isometric action of $SU(2) \times U(1)$ and $U(1) \times U(1) \times SU(2)$ respectively. We determine all the homogeneous, minimal hypersurfaces and explicitly compute the spectrum of their associated stability operators and determine their index.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Gherghel, Hari K. Kunduri

item.title: Twisted scalar curvature as a moment map
item.description: arXiv:2601.18141v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop the moment map theory of the twisted scalar curvature of a K\"ahler metric. Primarily, we introduce a coupled system of equations on a holomorphic submersion intertwining the twisted scalar curvature of a K\"ahler metric on the base and the fibrewise scalar curvature of a relatively K\"ahler metric on the total space. This resulting system can be viewed as producing the natural coupled metric geometry of holomorphic submersions, and we show that this system appears canonically as a moment map. The approach generalises to foliations, where we prove similar results.
item.dc:creator: Ruadha\'i Dervan, Thomas Murphy, Julius Ross, Lars Martin Sektnan, Xiaowei Wang

item.title: Flat Lorentzian Lie groups: A complete description
item.description: arXiv:2604.17292v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish a complete structural description of flat Lorentzian Lie groups, i.e., Lie groups endowed with a flat left invariant Lorentzian metric, thereby resolving a long-standing open problem in the theory of pseudo-Riemannian Lie groups. Our main result shows that any flat Lorentzian Lie group either admits a timelike parallel left-invariant vector field or is of Kundt type, and that in both cases the underlying Lie algebra falls into one of six explicit classes. A key ingredient of the proof is a refined analysis of the double extension process, which reveals that all flat Lorentzian Lie algebras arise - directly or in a generalized sense - from flat Euclidean ones. As a consequence, we obtain easily a complete classification in dimensions three and four, recovering and unifying several previously known partial results.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Boucetta

item.title: Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.23207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the variational problems associated with the $L^2$-norms of the normal and tangent curvature tensors for submanifolds immersed in a unit sphere. We define the critical points of these functionals under normal variations as Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds, for which we explicitly establish the Euler-Lagrange equations in terms of the second fundamental form. Furthermore, by investigating the focal submanifolds of OT-FKM isoparametric hypersurfaces, we construct infinitely many non-trivial examples of both Normal-Yang-Mills and Tangent-Yang-Mills submanifolds. Notably, the curvature tensors of these examples generally do not satisfy the classical Yang-Mills equations.
item.dc:creator: Jianquan Ge, Lixin Xiao, Wenjin Zhang

item.title: On Riemannian Geometry in Elastic Diffeology
item.description: arXiv:2608.01037v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Blohmann's tangent functor makes the category of elastic diffeological spaces a Cartesian tangent category in the sense of Cockett and Cruttwell. We use this structure to develop Riemannian geometry on elastic diffeological spaces. Following Cockett and Cruttwell, with additional axioms for scalar multiplication, we introduce connections, covariant derivatives and curvature; for a Riemannian metric we prove a Koszul formula and the uniqueness of the Levi-Civita covariant derivative. Our main result is a variational characterization of geodesics: if a full connection whose vertical part is Levi-Civita admits a geodesic flow fixing the zero section, then the critical paths of the energy functional are exactly the paths satisfying the geodesic equation, and regular length-minimizing paths are geodesics after constant-speed reparametrization. On elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, completeness of the geodesic spray yields such a flow and uniqueness of geodesics. The results apply to quotients of complete Riemannian manifolds by free isometric actions of countable groups, such as irrational tori, and, under a tangent-commuting hypothesis, to mapping spaces from a closed manifold into elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, including free loop spaces of complete Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Shiobara

item.title: Free boundary minimal annuli in convex balls
item.description: arXiv:2608.14679v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a $4$-parameter family of properly embedded genus-zero surfaces with at most two boundary components in a Riemannian $3$-ball. The construction is a free boundary analog of the canonical $5$-parameter family of surfaces on the $3$-sphere by Marques-Neves in the proof of Willmore conjecture. In the Euclidean unit ball, this family realizes the critical catenoid as a Simon-Smith min-max limit. As applications, we give an upper bound of Almgren-Pitts $4$-width $\omega_4(\mathbb{B}^3)$ by the area of the critical catenoid. Moreover, we prove the existence of at least three free boundary minimal annuli in any compact $3$-manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature and strictly convex boundary.
item.dc:creator: Dongyeong Ko, Guanhua Shao

item.title: Determination of all diffeomorphism invariant tensor fields on the space of smooth positive densities on a compact manifold with corners
item.description: arXiv:2609.34601v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It was proved in [3] that on a closed manifold of dimension greater than one, every smooth weak Riemannian metric on the space of smooth positive probability densities that is invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group is a multiple of the Fisher--Rao metric. Here we describe all purely covariant tensor fields of arbitrary order on the space of positive densities of a compact manifold with corners which are invariant under the action of the connected component of the diffeomorphism group. Finally, we classify the considerably fewer purely contravariant invariant tensor fields, describe the basic mixed contraction, and indicate the expected form of general invariant tensor fields.
item.dc:creator: Peter W. Michor

item.title: Analyticity and tautness of smooth Dupin submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.04679v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a smooth immersed Euclidean submanifold is locally Nash if it satisfies the Dupin condition on the regular part of its unit normal bundle. This condition is equivalent to the Morse-Bott property of all squared distance functions and, for compact connected embedded submanifolds, to tautness over $\mathbb{Z}_2$. No local finiteness assumption on the regular locus, or regularity assumption on its complement, is required. We also prove that, in each fixed Euclidean space, every compact connected smooth taut submanifold can be joined to one of finitely many representatives by a Nash isotopy through taut embedded submanifolds. In each fixed intrinsic dimension, we also obtain only finitely many diffeomorphism types admitting taut embeddings in Euclidean spaces. We first treat hypersurfaces by combining a dimension-dependent degree bound on proper Dupin pieces with a continuation argument using finite jets and resultants. An analytic Hessian criterion then gives the Morse-Bott property, and small tubes extend the conclusions to arbitrary codimension. The degree bound also provides uniform semialgebraic complexity.
