Together with the semialgebraicity of tautness in parameter families and Nash triviality, this yields the finiteness and deformation results. Classical classification theorems give further topological restrictions.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Wiesendorf

item.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.10132v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hasegawa

item.title: Negatively Curved Minimal Surfaces in the Round Four-Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.12238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct smooth closed embedded minimal surfaces with everywhere negative Gaussian curvature in the unit round four-sphere. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $m$, our construction gives a minimal surface $\Sigma_m$ of genus $m^2+1$ such that $\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma_m)\to 4\pi^2$ as $m\to+\infty$. This result yields a complete solution to Problem 101 in Yau's 1982 list of open problems.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Caniato

item.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21198v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Darvas, Kewei Zhang

item.title: Rotations, Shears, and Two-Generation on Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.27507v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every round sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, we exhibit two explicit smooth vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $Diff_0(S^n)$. By deleting one gradient component from the second generator, we obtain two explicit divergence-free vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $SDiff_0(S^n)$. In both cases two generators are minimal. The proof first generates the divergence-free vector fields using rotations, a linearly modulated rotational shear, and transverse vector spherical harmonics. On $S^2$ this reduces to the Hamiltonian/Poisson formalism; for $n\ge4$ irreducibility of the transverse harmonic spaces completes the degree-raising argument, while $S^3$ requires a separate treatment of its two curl eigenspaces. Adding one gradient field and using the divergence map then generates all smooth vector fields. Finally, a Casimir operator for a recovered copy of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ separates the components of the generating fields and compresses the natural finite generating families to two.
item.dc:creator: Dennis DeTurck

item.title: New inhomogeneous Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with large symmetry group
item.description: arXiv:2610.37102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study compact non-K\"ahler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds endowed with an automorphism group acting with cohomogeneity one. We prove that the Lie algebra of this group is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ or $\mathbb R^2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$, provided that the Bismut connection is not flat. In the first case, we explicitly describe all these structures up to homothety and biholomorphic isometry. We also construct explicit families of complete non-compact examples. The resulting non-Bismut-flat threefolds have non-constant scalar curvature and restricted Bismut holonomy $T^1\subset \mathrm{SU}(3)$, and include examples on $S^3\times S^3$ and complete examples on $S^3\times S^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$. Finally, we construct a smooth deformation of a Bismut-flat Samelson structure on $S^3\times S^3$ through non-Bismut-flat Bismut Hermitian-Einstein structures whose complex structures are not compatible with any Bismut-flat metric.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Podest\`a, Alberto Raffero

item.title: Levi-Civita's type theorem for projectively equivalent sub-Riemannian metrics on step 2 distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40288v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper extends the classical results of Eisenhart (1923) and Levi-Civita (1896) classifying pairs of germs of Riemannian metrics with the same geodesics, either as parametrized curves (affine equivalence) or as unparametrized curves (projective equivalence), to sub-Riemannian metrics on arbitrary step 2 distributions: at every stable point in the projective case and at every point in the affine case. This extends the results of Zelenko (2004) for contact and even-contact distributions and the affine result of Lin and Zelenko (2024) for step 2 distributions with ad-surjective Tanaka symbols; our projective result covers the ad-surjective case as well. In the affine case, we prove that if a sub-Riemannian metric admits an affinely equivalent metric that is not constantly proportional to it, then locally it is a product of two sub-Riemannian metrics. In the projective case, we prove the 2019 conjecture of Jean, Maslovskaya, and Zelenko on generalized Levi-Civita pairs; in particular, the distribution admits a product structure, the squares of its components are involutive, and the restrictions of the two metrics to each leaf of the corresponding foliation are conformal under the appropriate pullback. The proof uses a new graph-theoretic formalism, in which compatible moving frames are represented by the vertices and edges of certain graphs. As a byproduct, we introduce a new discrete invariant of step 2 nilpotent graded Lie algebras, the characteristic tuple. For left-invariant metrics on step 2 Carnot groups, this tuple is the growth of the osculating flags of the Jacobi curves of generic normal extremals, i.e., the lengths of the columns of their Young diagrams starting from the second column. The compatible graphs are used where this tuple is locally constant; the resulting bracket relations extend by continuity, so our classification requires no local constancy of the tuple.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Sinkule, Igor Zelenko

item.title: Koopman Regularization and Independent Koopman Eigenfunction Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2403.11302v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The geometry induced from a dynamical system dictates its latent structures, conservation laws, and intrinsic coordinates. This paper provides two procedures to extract the governing equations of a dynamical system from its samples, \acf{KR} and \acf{IKEA}. These procedures leverage the prior knowledge from the Koopman Eigenfunction Space. Both techniques extract a functionally independent set of Koopman Eigenfunctions, which are the intrinsic coordinates. Consequently, despite its finite cardinality, the governing equations are immaculately restored. Thus, the principle of parsimony is implemented. Samples can be taken either from a vector field or from orbits of the system. \acs{KR} extracts the governing law from samples of the vector field, and \acs{IKEA} extracts it from samples of trajectories of the system. Both algorithms are based on constrained optimization methods for learning the governing equations from sparse and corrupted samples of the vector field or trajectories. These procedures yield promising results in denoising, generalization, and dimensionality reduction and achieve better results than \acs{DMD}, \acs{EDMD}, \acs{PINN}, and \acs{SINDy} in dynamical system restoration.
item.dc:creator: Ido Cohen

item.title: The rigidity of Doyle circle packings on the infinite hexagonal triangulation
item.description: arXiv:2404.11258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Peter Doyle conjectured that locally univalent circle packings on the hexagonal lattice only consist of regular hexagonal packings and Doyle spirals, which is called the Doyle conjecture. In this paper, we prove a rigidity theorem for Doyle spirals in the class of infinite circle packings on the hexagonal lattice whose radii ratios of adjacent circles have a uniform lower bound in one fixed lattice direction. This gives a partial answer to the Doyle conjecture. Based on a new observation that the logarithm of the radii ratio of adjacent circles is a weighted discrete harmonic function, we prove the result via the Liouville theorem for discrete harmonic functions. Moreover, we establish a Ring Lemma for locally univalent circle packings with bounded degree, assuming that their carrier surfaces are the universal covers of $\mathbb{C}-\{0\}$, and the visual angles of all circles viewed from the origin are uniformly bounded away from $\pi$. This provides a new geometric sufficient condition for the rigidity of Doyle spirals.
item.dc:creator: Bobo Hua, Puchun Zhou

item.title: On an Iterative Scheme for the Spinorial Yamabe Equation on Manifolds with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2506.18546v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a fixed-point framework for non-linear boundary value problems for first-order elliptic operators on vector bundles, with primary application to the spinorial Yamabe and Brezis--Nirenberg equations. We prove existence and uniqueness of an $H^1$-solution under a smallness condition that is homogeneous under amplitude and operator scaling. The associated iterative scheme converges geometrically in $L^q$ and $H^1$, and the solution depends continuously on the harmonic representative of the boundary datum. Through bootstrapping, we obtain interior $C^{1,\alpha}$-regularity and boundary smoothness under Shapiro--Lopatinski conditions. The method is extended to families of small domains via rescaling to a fixed reference domain.
item.dc:creator: Eric Tr\'ebuchon

item.title: Genericity of ergodic measures on non-positively curved manifolds with flat strips
item.description: arXiv:2509.04916v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the geodesic flow defined on the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold with non-positive curvature. In the case of surfaces, Coud\`ene and Schapira proved that the existence of a flat strip prevents the set of ergodic measures from being generic in the space of invariant probability measures. We show the existence of a three-dimensional manifold that contains an embedded flat torus and where ergodicity is a generic property. More generally, Coud\`ene and Schapira proved that ergodicity is a generic property within the space of invariant probability measures defined on $\Omega_{NF}$, the set of non-wandering vectors whose orbits do not bound a flat strip. We introduce a larger set $\mathcal{R}_w$ where the same property holds, and we illustrate the extent of our findings using a famous example of a rank-one manifold attributed to Gromov.
item.dc:creator: Paul Mella

item.title: Starfield: Demand-Aware Satellite Topology Design for Low-Earth Orbit Mega Constellations
item.description: arXiv:2601.10083v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Low-Earth orbit (LEO) mega-constellations are emerging as high-capacity backbones for next-generation Internet. Deployment of laser terminals enables high-bandwidth, low-latency inter-satellite links (ISLs); however, their limited number, slow acquisition, and instability make forming a stable satellite topology difficult. Existing patterns like +Grid and Motif ignore regional traffic, ground station placement, and constellation geometry. Given sparse population distribution on Earth and the isolation of rural areas, traffic patterns are inherently non-uniform, providing an opportunity to orient inter-satellite links (ISLs) according to these traffic patterns. In this paper, we propose Starfield, a novel demand-aware satellite topology design heuristic algorithm supported by mathematical analysis. We first formulate a vector field on the constellation's shell according to traffic flows and define a corresponding Riemannian metric on the spherical manifold of the shell. The metric, combined with the spatial geometry, is used to assign a distance to each potential ISL, which we then aggregate over all demand flows to generate a score for each satellite's link selection. Inspired by +Grid, each satellite selects the link with the minimum Riemannian distance along with its corresponding angular links. To evaluate Starfield, we developed a custom, link-aware, and link-configurable packet-level simulator, comparing it against LAMP, +Grid, Motif, and Random topologies. For the Phase 1 Starlink, simulation results show up to a 30% reduction in hop count and a 15% improvement in stretch factor across multiple traffic distributions. Moreover, static Starfield, an inter-orbital link matching modification of Starfield, achieves a 15% improvement in stretch factor under realistic traffic patterns compared to +Grid. Experiments demonstrate Starfield's robustness under traffic demand perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Shayan Hamidi Dehshali, Tzu-Hsuan Liao, Shaileshh Bojja Venkatakrishnan

item.title: Kernel-Gradient Drifting Models
item.description: arXiv:2605.10727v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose kernel-gradient drifting, a one-step generative modeling framework that replaces the fixed Euclidean displacement direction in drifting models with directions induced by the kernel itself. Standard drifting is attractive because it enables fast, high-quality generation without distilling a large pretrained diffusion model, but its theory is currently understood mainly for Gaussian kernels, where the drift coincides with smoothed score matching and is identifiable. Our gradient-based reformulation exposes this score-based structure for general kernels: the resulting drift is the score difference between kernel-smoothed data and model distributions, yielding identifiability for characteristic kernels and a smoothed-KL descent interpretation of the smoothed drifting dynamics. Since kernel gradients are intrinsic tangent vectors, the same construction extends naturally to Riemannian manifolds and to discrete data via the Fisher-Rao geometry of the probability simplex. Across spherical geospatial data, promoter DNA and molecule generation, kernel-gradient drifting enables state-of-the-art one-step generation beyond the Euclidean setting without distillation. Code is available \href{https://github.com/jcarrascopollo/kgd_thesis}{here}.
item.dc:creator: Maria Esteban-Casadevall, Jorge Carrasco-Pollo, Max Welling, Jan-Willem van de Meent, Erik J. Bekkers, Floor Eijkelboom

item.title: On spherically symmetric Berwald vacuum solutions in Finsler gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.05427v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Berwald-Finsler spacetimes are Finsler spacetimes that are closest to pseudo-Riemannian geometry, as their canonical nonlinear connection defines an affine connection on spacetime. In this paper, we find the first exact, non-Ricci flat, $SO(3)$-symmetric Berwald solutions to the Finsler gravity vacuum equation. To this aim, we first select from all spherically symmetric Berwald spacetimes, the only class that admits flat Finsler spacetime structures, making it particularly suitable for future investigations of asymptotic flatness. Then, for this class, we completely solve the Finsler gravity vacuum equation, and find three families of solutions. In particular, we show that in Finsler geometry there exist $SO(3)$-symmetric, vacuum solutions that are not Ricci-flat. These solutions are promising candidates to model the gravitational field around compact objects, beyond their Riemannian description.
item.dc:creator: Nicoleta Voicu, Diana - Maria Birla, Christian Pfeifer

item.title: Magnetic cotangent groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2606.22288v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce magnetic cotangent groupoids on the cotangent bundle of a Lie groupoid using normalized cocycles, and characterize when magnetic symplectic forms are multiplicative on these groupoids. We show that $\mathbb{S}^1$-central extensions of Lie groupoids yield such structures via symplectic reduction. For a Kac--Moody extension, the resulting deformation connects the coadjoint and gauge action groupoids, which are not Morita equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Dadi Ni, Kaichuan Qi

item.title: A Geometric Derivation of the Einstein Equations from the Causal Action Principle
item.description: arXiv:2607.13871v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The causal action principle for causal fermion systems is analyzed for a minimizing measure whose support is assumed to have the structure of a smooth manifold $\tilde{M}$. The concept of osculating vacua is introduced. It is shown that the Lagrangian induces on $\tilde{M}$ a Lorentzian metric. Moreover, the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action imply that the Ricci tensor must satisfy the Einstein equations of General Relativity for an energy-momentum tensor given in terms of a power expansion in the regularization length. The gravitational coupling constant is found to be the square of the regularization length. Our methods provide a systematic procedure for deriving corrections to the Einstein equations. The paper includes a self-contained introduction to causal variational principles and the causal action principle. Most geometric structures (connection, Riemannian metric and curvature) are introduced and analyzed in the general setting of causal variational principles for an arbitrary dimension of $\tilde{M}$. The Lorentzian setting works only for causal fermion systems and is worked out only in four spacetime dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Felix Finster, Christoph Krpoun

item.title: Dirichlet symbols and the nonlinear wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.04666v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop the geometry of conformal mappings through Dirichlet operator symbols and the nonlinear wave equation. These symbols, introduced in the work of Hedenmalm and Shimorin (2020), are holomorphic functions on the bidisk associated with contractions on $L^2(\mathbb{D})$. For Grunsky operators, the nonlinear wave equation and the related Riccati equation induce a hierarchy of of differential relations along the diagonal. We use this jet hierachy to obtain alternative coordinates and a characterization of the manifold $\Sigma/\mathbb{C}$ of normalized exterior univalent functions modulo translations, without an explicit univalence test. This manifold may be viewed as an extension of the universal Teichm\"uller space beyond the quasicircle boundary setting. The diagonal jets also give rise to a hierarchy of \emph{diagonal series Schwarzian derivatives}. Already the fourth Schwarzian $S_4(\psi)$ leads to differential equations connected with the Weierstrass elliptic $\wp$ function and Painlev\'e I, revealing a comparison between the geometry of conformal mappings and that of complex tori. As a quantitative application of the framework, we interpret asymptotic variance through the Littlewood-Paley formula as an asymptotic density of quadratic nonlinearity energy under logarithmic averaging. We introduce Schwarzian asymptotic variance and obtain the upper bound $12.566563\ldots$ for its averaged squared hyperbolically normalized amplitude, in comparison with the classical pointwise bound $36$.
item.dc:creator: Ramlal Debnath, Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras from \v{S}evera bicomplexes
item.description: arXiv:2609.24781v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A \v{S}evera bicomplex is a bicomplex $(M,d_{0},d_{1})$ whose differentials $d_{i}$ are Grothendieck differential operators of order $\leq i$ with respect to a given $A$-module structure on $M$, where $A$ is a graded commutative algebra. One also requires that $(M,d_{0})$ admits a contracting homotopy $K$ that is a differential operator of the same order as $d_{0}$. Under suitable assumptions, the differential $d_{2}$ of the second page of the spectral sequence associated with $(M,d_{0},d_{1})$ is a Batalin-Vilkovisky operator on $E_{2}$, so that when $E_{2}$ is a free rank 1 $A$-module, the graded commutative algebra structure of $A$ is enhanced to a Gerstenhaber algebra structure, and the choice of a $d_{2}$-closed basis element for $E_{2}$ further enhances this to a Batalin-Vilkovisky algebra structure. The prototypical example of this construction is \v{S}evera's description of the Batalin--Vilkovisky algebra structure on the algebra of smooth functions of an odd symplectic manifold. Throughout the whole article we look at Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras through the lenses of Cartan calculus. Indications of a generalization to derived Cartan calculus are briefly discussed in the concluding section.

item.title: Edge-Connectivity versus Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.10559v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We systematically explore the relationship between edge-connectivity and Lin--Lu--Yau curvature for graphs. The intuition is that a connected graph with large Lin--Lu--Yau curvature should also have large edge-connectivity, and vice versa under suitable conditions. We prove that the edge-connectivity of a connected graph is bounded lower by the product of its minimum degree, its Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and the constant $\frac{3}{2}$. We also provide two lower bounds on the edge-connectivity of a graph that guarantee positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature, and discuss the sharpness of these bounds.
item.dc:creator: Ziming Zhou, Shenggui Zhang

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
item.description: arXiv:2610.32707v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -\Delta u=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that the equation admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove the compactness of the solution set for this equation by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is non-degenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set is finite. Our results also give a definite answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].
item.dc:creator: Wei Ji, Yixing Pu

item.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincar\'e prior that neither test decides
item.description: arXiv:2610.34309v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $\delta_F$ with bounded drift is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincar\'e inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincar\'e, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincar\'e class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
